title: The Rogue
observed_goal: Only a loading screen with the game title and the phrase “KINDLING THE VEIL” is visible in the frames; the active game objective was not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive.
observed_controls: The metadata records tests of Enter, Space, ArrowUp, w, ArrowRight, and holding ArrowRight + Space for 900ms; acceptance of any of them was not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive.
A click at the center of the canvas was recorded as start_action, but active game start is not confirmed by the frames.
observed_core_loop: The game loop was not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive; all four frames show only the loading state.
progress_feedback: A loading progress bar is visible in the frames and advances between frames; this is loading feedback, not game progress.
decisions_risk_reward: Decision-making, risk/reward, and in-game choices were not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive.
rewards: No reward or reinforcement system was not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive.
penalties_failure: No penalty, failure, damage, or loss state was not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive.
outcomes_replay: The outcome, win/loss, end of the run, and replayability were not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive.
onboarding: The only visible text at all four stages is “THE ROGUE” and “KINDLING THE VEIL”; no tutorial, control guide, or game introduction was not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive.
visual_audio_accessibility: Visually, a dark loading screen with a central logo and progress bar is visible. Audio, subtitles, accessibility settings, and control readability were not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive.
technical_clues: The page has a canvas sized 1280×800; this technical clue alone does not establish anything about mechanics or accepted input.
The console messages record 10 scripts, one stylesheet, image resources, and WebGL; this indicates only possible technical implementation/loading, not execution of the game loop.

The console records 404, 403, and 400 errors, a remote config error, and a WebGL software fallback warning; their effect on the game experience was not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive.
Changes in the progress bar and image between frames may result from animation or elapsed time; the metadata explicitly states that visual change does not prove input recognition.
transferable_principles: The loading state should provide clear visual feedback independent of actual game progress.
Input acceptance should be observable through a direct, interpretable change in game state, not merely a temporal difference between frames.
Control and objective instruction should be presented on a visible, testable screen before reliance on the core loop.
Recording the stage, source, and observation limitations is essential for separating direct evidence from design claims.
candle_climber_relevance: For Candle Climber, score/rank should reflect only skill and game outcome; this review provides no basis for a scoring mechanic from active gameplay.
No purchase or wallet should create an advantage; this principle is transferable as a design policy, not an observed feature of this game.
Avoid free brake and horizontal direction changes; adding a branching path requiring a new control should be presented only as a hypothesis requiring testing, not as a conclusion from this evidence.
Any proposed control scheme or loop for Candle Climber should be tested through independent execution and direct feedback; no specific mechanic can be derived from this loading screen.
do_not_copy: Do not reproduce the visual identity, logo, naming, page text, characters, sounds, or any specific asset.
Do not attribute a genre, level structure, multiplayer capability, ability selection, or enemies to the observed execution; these items appear only in the official card claim and were not playtested.
Do not interpret the progress-bar change as a response to keys or a click.
Do not infer a specific mechanic design from the loading frames or the game title.

evidence.claim: All four frames show a loading screen with the title “THE ROGUE,” the phrase “KINDLING THE VEIL,” and a progress bar; no active game screen, menu, or outcome is visible.
The stage text was recorded identically at all four stages: “THE ROGUE / KINDLING THE VEIL”.

The official card claims that the game consists of crafting four spells from seven elements, cursed rooms, increasingly numerous wardens, and solo, co-op, and arena modes; this claim was not confirmed by the game execution in the frames.
Enter, Space, ArrowUp, w, ArrowRight, and holding ArrowRight + Space for 900ms were tested, but their acceptance was not observed.
A visual change between frames was recorded, but the metadata itself warns that this change may be animation or elapsed time and does not prove input recognition.
A canvas with dimensions 1280×800 and WebGL/script resources were recorded; these are possible technical clues and do not establish the game loop.
404, 403, and 400 errors, a remote config error, and a WebGL software fallback warning were recorded; their effect on the game was not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive.

limitations: Only the metadata-and-capture-evidence file and the four submitted frames for this game were used. The capture has partial status and the late frame timed out. All frames are on the loading screen; therefore active gameplay, a repeatable loop, outcome, accepted controls, audio, accessibility, and the effect of technical errors were not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive. No web browsing or speculation about the game or hidden controls was performed.
